# PLAN-05: Role Agents Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use ultrapowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or ultrapowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship the fourteen lab roles as plugin agents that preload their skills, carry no tool allow-lists, and contain nothing project-specific.

**Architecture:** One `agents/<role>.md` per role, generated by hand from the current `claude_code_team/agents/<role>.md` with a fixed transformation: frontmatter rewritten to the supported fields, the shared "Operating rules" section dropped (it lives in `running-the-lab`), project-specific sentences replaced by the generic sentences listed per role, and the "Role toolkit" section kept with generic wording. `plugin.json` lists the fourteen files. A shell test enforces the frontmatter contract.

**Tech Stack:** Markdown agents with YAML frontmatter, bash test, `jq`.

**Spec:** `specs/2026-11-07-science-ultrapowers-design.md` — G4, D2, D7, Components "Agents", Constraints (plugin agent frontmatter).

**Sources:** Claude Code sub-agents reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md: supported fields `name, description, model, tools, disallowedTools, skills (≤32), color`; `initialPrompt`, `permissionMode`, `hooks`, `mcpServers` ignored in plugin agents; an explicit `tools` list is exhaustive; `AskUserQuestion` unavailable to subagents; nesting three deep by default), plugin components reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components.md: `agents/*.md`, manifest `agents` key replaces the default scan), both read 2026-11-07; the fourteen current agent files and `TEAM_SPEC.md` §7 (read 2026-11-07). Not checked: none.

## Global Constraints

- Frontmatter keys, exactly: `name`, `description`, `model: inherit`, `skills` (list), `disallowedTools` (list, may be `[]`), `color`. No `tools`, no `initialPrompt`, no `permissionMode`.
- `skills` always begins `science-ultrapowers:running-the-lab`, `science-ultrapowers:verifying-evidence-by-doi`, `science-ultrapowers:saving-artifacts`, `science-ultrapowers:remembering-for-the-lab`, then the role's own; at most 32 entries; every name exists under `skills/`.
- `disallowedTools` contains `Agent` for every role except `lab-project-manager` and `scientific-reviewer`.
- `description` starts with `Use` and is under 1,024 characters.
- No project-specific string (PLAN-01 gate) and none of these, matched as whole words, case-sensitive: the source project's name, the dataset name, the data-task id, `TIK`, `Springer`, `sn-jnl`, `DistilBERT`, `BERT`, `ViT`, `UPF`, `GFU`, `CIFM`, `ACT`, `Optuna`, `uv run`, `ruff`, `mypy`, `bandit`, `config_validator`, the funder's name, the data-task id.
- Colours from the supported set: red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, cyan.

## Review Focus

1. A role whose `skills` list names a skill that does not exist loads with a silent gap: Task 3's test resolves every entry to a folder.
2. A writer role with `Agent` allowed can spawn a reviewer of its own work: Task 3's test asserts `Agent` in `disallowedTools` for the twelve roles.
3. A description that summarises the role's workflow steers the main session to skip the agent body: Task 3's test rejects descriptions containing `then` chains longer than 300 characters (crude, but catches the pattern).
4. The manifest `agents` key replaces the default scan; a file present in `agents/` but missing from `plugin.json` never loads: Task 3's test compares the two lists.
5. A role body that still says "You cannot ask the user questions directly" but points at a removed section: Task 1's template moves that line into `running-the-lab` and the body keeps only the role's own duties.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

`test-agents.sh`: for each `agents/*.md`: frontmatter has exactly the six keys in order; `model: inherit`; no `tools:`; no `initialPrompt`; every `skills` entry `science-ultrapowers:<x>` has `skills/<x>/SKILL.md`; list length ≤ 32; the first four entries are the common four; `disallowedTools` contains `Agent` unless the file is `lab-project-manager.md` or `scientific-reviewer.md`; `description` starts with `Use` and is under 1024 characters; `color` in the allowed set; the body contains none of the forbidden words in Global Constraints; the body contains `## Role toolkit` only where the source had one (hard-code the nine names: supervisor, methods, data-evaluation, experiments, documentation, paper, academic-reviewer, scientific-reviewer, research-engineer). `jq -r '.agents[]' .claude-plugin/plugin.json | sort` equals `ls agents/*.md | sed 's#^#./#' | sort`. ## Execution record (2026-11-08)

Executed by an Opus 5.5 orchestrator; Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 implementers wrote the agents and the test from one shared brief and never committed; the orchestrator read every agent against its source, fixed what the reading found and committed in task order. A fresh Fable 5.1 reviewer judged the branch ready to merge (0 Critical, 1 Important, 5 Minor); every finding was fixed in one pass, each with a check that failed first.

- R2, R15: role text fits any paper, project or thesis: "your human partner" for the person, no doctoral-only standard, a monitoring committee rather than a thesis committee.
- R3: the Role toolkit names its skills as `science-ultrapowers:<skill>` and points at the vetting record in `research_lab/09_skill_vetting/`.
- R6: descriptions are double-quoted YAML (most contain ": ").
- R8, R16: `test-agents.sh` checks the whole file, plus resolution, bare names, the `When to invoke` section, the description pointer, the generality strings, the toolkit's vetting pointer and running-the-lab's main-session line.
- R10: plugin-dev's validate-agent.sh stops at its first warning under `set -e`; `claude plugin validate .` is the structural check.
- R11: the research engineer keeps the general duty to fix prioritised defects.
- R13: the manifest gains only the `agents` key (alphabetical), inserted as text.
- R14 (your human partner's request): every agent body has a `## When to invoke` section ending in a `Not this role` line, and every description points to it. Before and after the change, role agents asked for out-of-scope work refused (before 4/4, after 5/5, one after-run also offering to draft on re-dispatch).
- Final fixes: running-the-lab's main-session sentence names only `lab-project-manager` and `scientific-reviewer` (the twelve others keep `disallowedTools: [Agent]` under `--agent`), and every role never opens a folder the project brief marks out of scope; PLAN-06's project brief gains the slots the agents point at; docs/testing.md lists the new tests.
